# Chapter Seven: The Gathering Faith

Traveling Priest

Marcus sat upon the rock looking out over the landscape, the small group of mages had been walking for close to ten miles. His mind was a room full of voices, never ending lectures, everytime he formed a thought whispers, yells voices that were not his would rise up in his mind. He did not speak, would not speak focusing all his energy to calm and understand those voices that now resided within his head. Though his mind was cluttered he could hear everything, every sound of the birds chirping, the leaves rustling and the conversations that took place around him as his friends worried and unsure argued relentlessly.

“Maelen, we don’t know what effect this will have on him, never has a transfer been done without the supervision of a master healer, it takes years to prepare for this and Ablion simply dumped his entire knowledge base and htat of the previous three Archivists into his head. Albion had Idedic memory Maelen, do you have any idea what that can do to a person” Patrice said her tone severe as he tried to make her lover understand the situation.

“Marcus, I know your in there, can you answer me?” Came the worried voice of Dara next to him, he simply stared straight ahead, the voices yelling, lecturing, explaining as Patrice talked information and definitions unraveled in his head, explaining the procedure and what had happened. Closing his eyes, he concentrated on this, tried to follow the train of thought. As the aged voice of Master Albion echoed off of the internal walls of his mind. “The transfer is a delicate process, it takes a neural map of the donor’s mind and then the same is done to the recipient, this allows the memories to be translated from one person to another, without the ability to encode them to the pattern of the recipients brain, both parties will go mad” the lecture began. Marcus blocked all other stimuli, allowing the information to flow from him, almost as if listening to a lecture for the first time, except every sentence was something he didn’t know and was intimately familiar with at the same time. It was by far the strangest feeling he had ever had.

“Though the process does allow for the translation, there is a period where the brain digests the information, until it has fully processed it, the information will seem forieng to the recipient, during this time there can be side effects that manifest itself physically, though they are different in each person” continued the voice. He felt Dara still holding his hand and he could hear Patrice and Maelen still arguing in hushed tones as he sat there, unmoving and unresponvice. He wasn’t comatose, at least he didn’t think he was but the effect this was having on his mind and his body was strange at the very least he thought.

Marcus thought back to the Order, to the dragon he had known how to activate it, known it was a combination, but Albion hadn’t known, at least not directly he had been close to understanding how the runes worked, how they were ordered and how to power them to activate the guardian he reflected. There was so much knowledge he had access to that it threatened to drown him. In fact he thought it was too much, he couldn’t concentrate on one thing, couldn’t focus because everytime he tried it was like a tsunami would crash against his brain bringing with it trains of thought and tangends on any number of topics that might be included within one question he thought of.

How am I supposed to use this he thought and once again the voices rose in a chorus, each one answering and offering opinions and suggestions, but it was too much he couldn’t make out one voice or one person or one answer. Closing his eyes, he cleared his mind, trying to quiet the voices for a moment. His head ached a deep thrumming, but mercifully concentrating on that sent the voices away.

“We have no idea what kind of state he is in, for all we know he is catatonic, and his mind has been damaged beyond anyone’s ability to repair it” Patrice hissed. Marcus turned his head; he could hear Dara gasp as he did. Doing his best to maintain his concentration on the ache, on the rhythim of the pain he opened his mouth. “I am okay, just need time” he said flatly and then concentrated fiercly clearing his mind before the voices could rise up again to give him estimates nd explanations of his response.

Everyone went still and turned, Maelen looked unbelieving that Marcus had even spoke, as if the event had been a trick of his hearing. “Did he just…” he began and Both Patrice and Dara nodded. “He is there” Dara said and Marcus could hear the smile on her face, his eyes closed as he continued to simply concentrate on the drum that beat against the inside of his head, causing him to wince in pain, but the quiet was worth it, worth the pain and worth the discomfort. Marcus continued to sit there, Patrice, Maelen and Dara trying desperately to get him to speak.

Sitting there he looked at them pleading at them when finally, he was forced to speak. “give me time” he simpy said and his mind exploded with voices causing him to wince. The three stood there watching him, at least Maelen seemed to understand, they made camp giving Marcus the time he needed while Dara never leaving his side whispered words of encouragement throughout the night, she stood sentry and the small part of Marcus’s mind that was his felt guilty, this woman obviously cared but all he could think of was Orah…

The next morning Marcus awoke to blessed silence “About Time” he croaked, bracing himself for the inevitable he thought about the runic language. This time however his mind did not overpower him, instead, like a read dissertation that he had put down, he could recall an incredible amount of information as if he was the one who had studied it. In fact his knowledge was so in depth and so natural he tried to recall which of the knowledge was actually his and couldn’t. “How are you feeling?” Came Maelens concerned voice and as he looked over he smiled at his old teacher, thought this close to the episode with Albion it was muted and sad “I am okay, I feel more like me Maelen, Im sorry I was out of it, it was, well it was hell” he finished and the old man smiled and handed him the water skin “We have very little supplies so this will have to do for now” he finished Dara returned, at some point she had left, going into the woods and returning with food, of course using Maelen’s trick he thought with a smirk.

The group ate rabbit and ate well as they sat around the small fire “Where are we going?” Maelen asked the group Marcu had stopped eating thirty minutes ago and now tolerated poking and prodding from Patrice who would not take no for an answer. “You have just undergone an incredinly strssfull trauma to your mind, I will be monitoring this, so you need to get used to it” she finished pushing Marcus’s hand away when he tried to pause her. Marcus thought about it, more information then he had ever known about the territories and the surrounding area was quickly available to him and he filtered through it, looking to see if anything useful might present itself. “We can go north, the Barrens are no man’s land and the Empress has no hold on them, it would take us away from Lusor and Dever both of which seem to have soldiers looking for me also, I am unknowningly involved in some political gambit and I truly have no wish to find out what they wish to do with me” he finished looking at the three Mages.

Patrice thought about it and after a few moments looked to Maelen and nodded “He is right, there aren’t many places we can go and the Barrens are neutral, if we can allow the outcasts to allow us to stay, we will be safe at least for a while, I am sure the Empress will not leave the territory alone for long” Patrice finished and Maelen agreed. Everyone looked to Dara who stared back “I have no idea where to go, if Marcus says Barrens, then lets go” she said simply her Raven hair still mussed from the hard night of watching Marcus, looking at her her reguarded the young girl, young he thought she was only a year younger then he was, why then did he feel so much damn older “Because you had the memories and training of four elders of the Order dumped into your head” he whispered to himself.

Dara looked at him cocking her head “What?” she asked, and he waved her off. “Its nothing, just talking to myself” he finished and then caught the look everyone gave him, somewhere between suspicion and alarm. “Im not answering myself, so please don’t worry” he followed up his annoyance showing through in his tone. “Alright, North it is, but we will have to use old trails and stay away from villages and popular market routes, I do not want to run into the damn soldiers, its not healthy to be a mage right now” he finished and Marcus shook his head “I agree we need to stay away from most of them, but I need to check mine, I have friends and I will know what happened to them before we move north, if we can help them Maelen, we will” Marcus said, leveling a gaze at his old teacher, At first Maelen and Patrice looked to protest but he guessed they caught the look on his face, he would not be swayed and any attempt was fultile, they gave in with a resined nod. Getting everyone’s attention Patrice moved to the center of the small group, standing next to the fire she looked around “We will need to stop at, at leas one village, we have no supplies, no weapons and I will need to pickup medicines, Marcus may look ok, but he has gone through an incredible trauma, I need to treat him using the same tequniques we do when a guild leader does a transfer” she finished and Maelen looked about to protest and then caught the look in his lover’s eye and deflating he simply nodded “But we will need to be careful” he followed up.

“This has been done before?” Marcus asked, and just as he did the answer was in his head “Yes Marcus, this is a common occurrence, when a guild leader is close to death, he will choose his successor and they perform the transfer so the knowledge of the previous generation is not lost. Usually its done within the confines of the Order and the recipient has at least two weeks of rest before venturing out, unfortunately we do not have that luxury, but I will be damned if that means we are going to ignore the normal medications to help ease the transfer” she finished and marcus looked around the group “I feel fine Master Patrice” he said and she shot him a disapproving look. “Of course, you do Marcus, that is until that moment when you don’t, this is nothing to play around with and I will not ignore my duty” she finished, and the tone told everyone that this subject was absolutely closed for debate.

Cleaning up the camp the group setout, using the sun to guide them as they headed North, they stayed within the woods ensuring that they stayed away from the market and farming trails, once a patrol passed them and they were forced to hunker down until they passed.

Moving on, they walked for most of that day, but as evening approached they spotted a village, this one looked promising, it was a tiny place of only about four buildings within the village center, too small to have a keep for worship it looked as if the soldiers either had overlooked it or they had not reached this far. The group stood outside under the cover of the trees watching for a good few hours, ensuring that no soldiers showed up or were present but hiding. “It will feel good to sleep in a bed” Marcus said eyeing the Stags Inn sign, every window lit up as the locals, now finished with there day came drown their sorrows and pain.

The small group walked into the village and made their way to the small inn, inside they could hear the laughters and music as the townsfolk held their nightly celebration to blow off steam from the workday. “Hey, hold on, who are you?” came a suspicious voice behind them, the group turned to find a small old man in what looked like an ancient piece of rusted armor and a warrior’s pole, that had defeintely seen better days. “We are weary travelers looking for a place to lay out head for the night and pickup supplies in the morning, then we will be on our way” Patrice said gently.

The old man looked them over suspiciously. “I guess that would be fine, you don’t look like soldiers and definitely don’t look like demons” he said warily. Marcus cocked his head “demons?” he asked and the man shook his head “Where you been boy, this land is lousy with em, the Empress has called forth the minions of mephis and she sends them after the villages, haven’t you heard, every village from here to Lusor. Slaves all of them” he sid shaking his head. “Eventually they will come for us, but we will fight, we aren’t going be the Empresss slaves, we work hard, its our land and our town” he continued and Marcus heard the resolve in his voice, but he also knew what the Empress could bring down on these people, he didn’t want to see them crushed “Why not go north, there might be protection there, at the very least you will be out of her reach” he said, almost pleading with the old man.

The tin soldier simply shook his head stubbornly “This is our town, no one, not even some jumped up polywog of a Empress is going to scare us away” he finished, and Marcus could hear the pride in his voice. This man would not run, he wouldn’t leave his home or his people but that also meant they would die, they would fight bravely but the soldiers were many and well trained, Marcus thought well of this old man but if this group of villages expected to stand against the likes of the Empresss guard and win, then they were lying to themselves. Turning the group headed to the inn.

Entering the inn Marcus squinted his eyes at the acrid smoke that permeated the room, the smell of yeast and fresh sawdust heady in the air the group crossed to a far corner and took seats at one of the few empty tables in the place. “How is it, with everything we have seen there are still places like this, untouched by the Empress’s wrath” Marcus whispered looking amazed at the happy residents of this small village.

Maelen glanced over his shoulder reguarding the group with a smile. “Because this place is small and the Empress needs to secure the larger villages and cities before she can move on something that is so below the radar in the way of territory economy” he said and the whispered in Marcus’s head agreed, expounding upon the percentages of wheat and grain a village like this would produce. Marcus did his best to ignore it, but it was not easy he reflected flagging down a plumb bar maiden with a permanent smile and well-endowed cleavage. Her worn dress that looked pinker than red worn a little tight better to increase the tips Marcus thoughts with a smirk.

They ordered a round of drinks and a meal as the group eyed the bar, they had seen enough destruction in the past month that even now, in this place they half expected soldiers to spring out of the well-worn woodwork. “If my memory serves, this is the last small village we will find between here and the border, so eat up and rest, I don’t think we will be seeing any more taverns after this” Maelen said his face dour as he looked at Patrice, the woman running her hand through the old Teachers white hair in an attempt to calm him. Maelen had take there exodus from the Order hard, he had been there for nearly two decades in service to its ideals only to find out that even his beloved order was in league with the Empress. Marcus eyed him, knowing his very core was shaken by the realization and he would have to process that in his own time. Despite the feeling of celebration and laughter that surrounded the little inn, Marcus was guilty at his feeling of resentment towards the patrons of this place. He had lost everything, been chased over the entire territory and even now hunted like an animal and yet, looking around these people didn’t seem to have a care in the world. His logical mind was happy for them, happy that the death and destruction had not touched their lives. But there was another part that somehow felt their celebration was an affront to the friends and loved ones lost in this land.

Taking a breath, he pushed that feeling down, it was unfair to blame these people. “Are you okay?” Dara asked gently and Marcus turned to see her dark eyes wide and worried as she looked to him. He smiled weaked and nodded “just tired” he lied, there was no point in trying to explain feelings that would make him sound like a self-centered ass he thought. Dara moved a little closer to Marcus and he was more then aware of her body pressing against him. She had been doing that a lot recently, always finding a way to sit next to him, ride next to him and always just a little too close. He didn’t move, but part of him felt guilt Orah was not that long dead and he still mourned for the woman who was the center of his life and he wasn’t ready to move on, wasn’t ready to pursue anything new, even if it was with a exceedingly attractive, sweet and intelligent woman who obviously had feelings for him. Marcus did his best to ignore her closeness and looking up could see Maelen’s knowing eyes as he sat there reguarding the two of them. He nodded and a small smile shown for a moment before disappearing again, he obviously approved but they had more important things to think about then young love he mused.

The lights dimmed as a couple of new performers took the stage, the patrons clapping and yelling as the man and woman bowed “Whats going on?” Marcus asked, craning his neck to get a better view. “That’s our local superstars Morin and Mari velen, they play the ancient songs, everyone loves them” the waitress said, delivering another round of drinks as she gushed over the brother and sister team. Marcus nodded and watched as the patrons quieted down everyone looking to the stage as the young man pulled out an odd string instrument, one that laid flat. It looked like a box that tapered at one end, something like eighteen strings wired across it, the woman pulled something that looked like the cousin of a tambourine with a stick attached and the two began to strum out a beat. The two musians were aided by the crowd as they slammed their glasses against the wooden tables in time to the beat.

Finally, the man a deep baritone with a theatrical growl began to sing and Marcus’s head snapped up. It was sung in there native language but as his mind translated the words, he knew the song, knew it well in fact as the man sang “Im not the one who’s so far away..” and the glasses slammed in time Marcus’s head began bobbing as he whispered the words in time with the man as he continued to croon Godsmack’s Voodoo.

The small group stayed until well into the early morning, enjoying the music and the company of the energetic crowd, it had been too long since Marcus had even witnessed a good time much less had one. Walking out of the inn they walked back to the stalls as the young boy half asleep began to pull their horses and prepare them. Marcus handed the young man two silverlings and tussled his hair as he continued to hum the music from the night a rare smile on his face. The foursome rode from the village as the patrons shambled their way home to prepare for another hard day of work.

Leaving the village behind Marcus breathed in the cool night air, closing his eyes as he enjoyed the brisk night against his skin for once his mind not occupied with worry of the Empress or the Mages or the solders. The group rode towards the North, allowing themselves a good distance from the village before they decided to settle for the night and sleep.

Marcus awoke with a start as a hand grasped his arm hard enough to cause him to wince, despite the grogginess of sleep, his eyes opened and he looked around noticing that it was still dark, not even the rays of early morning had begun to creep up over the land. “Whats wrong” he whispered and felt the hand loosen on his arm. “Something is out there” Dara whispered bringing her mouth close to his ear enough so that the expulsion of breath tickled. “Where is Maelen” he asked and looked, spotting the older man almost instantly as he crouched near the large trunk of a tree. Then Marcus heard it, the distinct snapping of branches and a shuffling coming from beyond where Maelen had hidden.

He spotted Patrice behind yet another tree as they both maintained there hiding spots trying to get a look at whatever had decided to disturb their camp. He tapped Dara and pointed to a fallen tree and two crawled for cover. One there Marcus brought himself up enough to peer over the tree but aside from the noise before, he could make out nothing. The darkness preventing him from even seeing beyond twenty feet or so. “Did anyone get a look at it” he whispered still trying to gain at least a glance at what it might be, half of him was trying to convince himself it was a racoon or something while another side began to whisper about ghosts and Lord Seers with powers.

“No, but whatever it is, its large” she said and Marcus was about to ask her how she had come to this conclusion when another sound came from the wooded area, a shriek rebounded off of the trees as a chill went up Marcsus’s back and sweat broke out on his body. This was no Racoon he thought. His mind turned over trying to find a way out of this, a way to get everyone free of the camp without alerting the thing that now stalked them. The whispering in his brain became louder as idea after idea was dismissed. “This isn’t helping” he thought finally standing up “What are you doing” dara hissed fear dripping off of her words. “Someone has to draw it out, otherwise it is going to try and pick us off” he said the words not his as he stepped from behind the tree, shooting a glance at Marcus and Patrice willing them to stay there.

His rational mind was screaming at him to run, to give up with stupid plan and just bolt, Marcus held his ground, his arms were shaking with fear, so he crossed them, he didn’t want Dara to see him like that. Taking three steps forward he began to whistle a tune, it took him a few times to wet his lips enough to do it, the fear having driven the salive from his mouth but after a few attempts he stood there, eyeing the woods as he simply whispered. Out of the corner of his eye he could see the looks that Patrice and Maelen were giving him. It was as if he had simply gone mad and they were deciding if anything they could do.

Then all thoughts were driven from his mind, emerging from the darkness were two glowing blue orbs sliding along close to the ground but moving towards Marcus’s right. At first he thought it was some kind of cat, maybe a puma he wondered and then it crossed into a beam of weak moonlight, but not weak enough as Marcus got his first look at the unearthly screamer. It looked like a man, well mostly except it moved on all fours, its skin was death white and the eyes glowed a phosphorescent blue. It slid a few more feet, half in and half out of the beam as it stopped and crouched there reguarding him.

He watched as the creature cocked its head like a curious dog, neither one moving as they simply looked at each other. He could still see his comrades out of the corner of his eye and willed them to be still. Maybe this thing will go away Marcus thought as it continued to reguard him. Then slowly the creature uncoiled itself coming to stand on two legs and as it did, its mouth opened wide, wider then should have been possible as it unleashed another chilling scream. It took two steps and was it smiling he thought trying to get a better look in the dark. The creature made a casual motion with its hand and before Marcus could think his own hand shot out and he looked over surprise on his face as a sharp branch hung in the air, suspended by his power. He looked from the branch to the creature, its eyes narrowed, and it hissed at Marcus, launching itself into the air, the creature hung there as it cleared the thirty or fourty feet arcing towards Marcus.

Without a thought, without even a plan, his hand came up, power flashing into his body and with a motion he slammed the creature plucking it out of the air and sending it straight into the ground. He heard the bones break as it struck. His mouth stood open in surprise “What the..” he began but the creature was already up coiling itself it launched directly at Marcus he brought up his arm trying to cover his face when he heard a thumb and the creature dropped to the ground hitting his legs.

Marcus looked down to see a metal pole sticking out of the creature, on one end sat a carved dragon claw with a glowing crystal. Maelen walked over, pulling the weapon out of the screamer and now he could see the blade it held. He stared as if in shock as Maelen wiped the blade on the black robe of the creature and then taking another one exactly like it, pushed them together to form a small staff. “What the hell is that?” Marcus asked, his mind unable to focus on anything as he simply stared at it. “This is a mage blade, one day I will train you on it” he said with a grim smile as he checked the thing on the ground. “Its dead” he said, and the girls came out to study it.

Once Maelen had named it, Marcus knew in detail what it was as pictures and positions and fighting styles shot through his head. It was a versatile weapon, one that could be used to direct power, fight an enemy or defend oneself both physically and magically.

Every picture and sentence giving Marcus a better idea of them and by the time the voices had settled he was quite impressed with the ingenuity and innovation of those who had created it.

“What the hell is that thing?” Dara asked stepping up behind Marcus as she peered around him to look at it. “I don’t know but if whatever Albion did to me hadn’t stepped in, then I would be dead right now” Marcus said and shot Maelen a grateful stare “Thank you, you kind of saved my life” he said and Maelen smiled “you would have done the same” he finished and the group crouched down to look upon the creature.

The sat around well away from the area where Patrice had cut the creature open and was now examining it closely, she had been at it for hours and now the sun had come up and day getting warmer as they looked over once in a while to see Master Patrice still closely examining the thing that had attacked them. Finally, she got up coming over to the group. “So, what is it?” Maelen asked, his eyes wandering over to the mess that now lay on the ground twenty feet away. Patrice shook her head “Not what, who, it’s a person or was” she said her eyes looked angry. “Whoever did this, twisted this person using magic, then embedded crystals into there body, though I am not quite sure what for. But know this Maelen, whoever did this was trying to recreate the process that gave you and Marcus your powers” she finished the last statement catching both men’s attention. “What are you talking about?” Marcus said not liking where this was going. “The blood is full of an unknown component; it looks as if someone had been transfusing it into this person for close to a year or more. Unfortunately, they weren’t experts in genetics, so they opted to simply introduce the compound directly into the blood stream and then from the look of it, expose them to high amounts of radiation.

What you are looking at is a human mutation brought on by someone’s experiments to create powerful mages” she finished, and Marcus could hear the disgust in her tone. “We know who that someone is” Marcus stated looking to everyone in the group. “We have all heard the rumors of the Lord Seer’s and their demons” he finished and pointed to the creature.

“This is her doing, If I am right, the Lord Seer’s weren’t as powerful when they started, she did something to them” he began, and his mind exploded as the voices began to lecture and theorize. Closing his eyes, he willed them quiet when he opened them, he could see the worried look from everyone in the group. “Im okay, just sometimes it gets a little loud in my head” he said half joking.

“Marcus, you are still not fully healed and we have no idea what kind of side effects from the stress of traveling will do to the transfer or how it will manifest itself in you, just please be careful and keep me informed” Patrice said gently. Marcus nodded and went back to staring at the creature.

“Does no one want to ask the two big questions; I mean we have been sitting here for hours and not one of you have asked where it came from and was it alone” Maelen said annoyed at the group. Marcus looked at him for a moment “Well good questions to ask a few hours ago, I am going to guess it was alone because we are not sitting here with soldiers or more of those things all over us, as for where it came from, I am guessing it reports to a Lord Seer somewhere” he finished.

“Reguardless, I have no real idea what those crystals embedded inside the thing does, so for all I know whoever this thing reports to knows its dead and might have already sent out patrols to find out what happened, either way, we need to get out of here” Patrice said and everyone nodded. It took the group only about ten minutes to get everything together and ensure they had wiped away all evidence that a camp had been here.

“Marcus” Maelen began motioning him to follow as the two stepped away from the woman. “Tomorrow we will be at the old farmhouse and then to the village, are you sure you want to do this, the stories I have heard. You might not like what you find” he finished gently but Marcus knew what he was getting at, they had come across more then one village and seen the people hanging or dead. “I have to know, if I can help them what kind of a person would I be if I left them there” he finished and Maelen nodded.

“Okay, lets do it then” he said and then called the girls over as the group began to walk north again, heading back to where it began for Marcus.

They walked in silcene the rest of the day as each person thought about the thing that had once been a person, Marcus did not truly understand the measures the Empress qould take to complete her goal until that moment. He had never understood what “Power Mad” meant. But now, in light of everything he had seen, in light of what had happened to the people of this land he truly understands that term now.

He waa coming to the realizing that this woman needed to be stopped, that he might be one of the few people with enough power to accomplish it. This was not a line of thinking he wanted to follow, he wasn’t a damn hero if anything he was the victim, every turn someone had been hunting him, someone had wanted to use him for their own ends. Even those who wanted to capture him to bleed him dry for the betterment of something he thought bitterly. Who did he think he was, did he really think he was the person to bring out change like that, like he was some kind of superhero? No, that was better left to people who, well weren’t him he thought shaking his head.

The mood of the group was dark for the rest of the day and well into the night. By the next morning Marcus realized no one had really spoken two words to each other after the screamer. Shaking his head he looked around at his compatriots, they all had haunted looks in their eyes, everyone of them he guessed had come to the same realization about the Empress, this was not going to stop, this was not going to peter out but instead get worse, The Empress would see every person under her rule enslaved or experimented on or killed it if even remotely furthered her goals. Black Empress was an apt nickname he thought as he collected his things and looked on as the group joined him.

Today he would be back at Orah’s, the first time he had seen the farm since she had died, he thought. Part of him had no desire to see it, but there was another part that had to, he had to know what happened to his friends and he had to say his goodbyes to the woman he loved. Maelen might have buried her elsewhere he thought. But everything that was Orah was there at the farm, every memory, every thought and ever happy time were all there. If he was to say his final goodby, then there was no better place he reflected as the group walked on through the woods. Maelen leading the way.

It was around noon when Marcus started to recognize landmarks and trails, realizing they were now very close to Orah’s farm he began to get nervous and worried. Finally, they came over a bend and looking down the hill there stood the charred ruin of the house that Marcus swore he would spend the rest of his life in. It looked different now he thought as the group walked down the hill, his eyes never leaving the home, he studied the blackened walls and collapsed roof as they got closer to it. The pens were mostly gone, anything of value had probably been taken long ago, but the house or what was left of it, still stood there. Reaching the gate Maelen held the women back, nodding to Marcus to go on. “He needs to do this alone” he said to them as they waited for him to return. Marcus was not listening to them, his eyes looking over the space where the door had been, the door that he had knocked on one desperate night and a woman who didn’t need to, saved his life not once but twice. Once when she had opened the door, the seond time when she told him she loved him.

The tears came without warning he didn’t try to stop them as he walked into the ruin of the house. Every place he looked he could see her smiling at him, see her looking with those eyes filled with love and affection for him. Moving into the bedroom his legs gave out as he sat there sobbing the ruins of the bed, still like it had been that day he had found her burning and dead. Throwing back his head he screamed and screamed letting the anger and the utter sadness expel from his body.

Marcus yelled until his voice went hoarse, his throat feeling like someone had poured molten lava down it. The tears were gone, he had no more left as he simply sat there, staring at the bed, wondering how his life would be today had he not gone to town, had he stayed here and protected her, been there when she most needed him. After all the pain and sadness, the one overriding emotion that scrathed at his soul was the guilt. Part of him felt he had abandoned her, had gone seeking answers trying to find out things that now seemed unimportant. The only thing that had been important, the only thing that mattered had died that day he thought looking at the bed and wincing from the physical pain he felt at letting her down and not protecting her.

“I am so sorry Orah, I left you and I should have been here, I should have protected you, instead I was out chasing answers that didn’t matter, the only thing that did matter was here” he said, fresh tears rolling down his cheeks as he knelt praying at the altar to the only god that had ever shown him a greater power in the universe then man, Love.

After a time, Marcus slowly and unsteadily rose to his feet, stumbling out of the house, he turned to take one last look. He would not come back here; he would never see this place again for now it held nothing for him. Turning his back on it a final time he walked unsteadily down to the gate his friends waiting as he exited the property and the group began walking towards the village.

Dara walked close to him, not talking but just offering what comfort she could with her proximity. Marcus did not comment on it, nor did he really notice, his mind was a storm of emotion and guilt engulfed his mind and soul as he walked. Finally, they came upon the wall of the town. Marcus remembering the first time he saw the upended trees that made the protective outer wall of the small village. ‘Not everyone lives with honor’ Orah had said as if she were standing right there and Marcus was seeing those beautiful eyes and the smile that always sent lightning through his heart. He watched the image fade, replaced by the cold of loss. “How do you want to do this?” Came Maelen’s voice breaking into Marcus’s moment, taking a breath he turned and reguarded his mentor and friend. “This is my call, my responsibility, I am going to go in and you guys will wait out here. If there is a problem or the town is guarded, then at least you can get away. I won’t have people dying for my stupidity” he finished and Maelen smiled a little “At least your recognizing that its stupid” he answered. But Marcus could hear the stress in his voice.

Leaving the small group behind Marcus approached the open gates, the errie silence putting him on edge as he reached out with his mind, searching for danger. Nothing was present, not even a person he realized opening his eyes and slowly walking in.

Where had all the people gone, he wondered, or the guards for that matter. It was mid day so it was possible from the rumors that everyone had been led out to work, but wouldn’t they still guard the village he wondered, passing through the gates and into the village courtyard. Something had Marcus on edge, but he couldn’t put his finger on it as the voices whispered urgently trying to get his attention. Tamping them down he took a few more steps, looking around at the closed and empty buildings surrounding him. Walking towards the center he finally came around to view the side of the keep, where he had spent many a happy moment with Veric and stopped cold. “Shit” he whispered wincing as he looked up to see a makeshift gallows and his friend swinging from one of the ropes, the other was occupied by the mage who ran the crystal shop, both still looked fairly fresh but the wounds over there face and exposed upper bodies showed extensive beatings. Someone had tortured them before hanging them there he thought.

Again, he felt on edge, something wasn’t right, and he couldn’t’ put a finger on it. Reaching out again he allowed his senses to travel further, searching for any sign of life in the small village. He could sense nothing, absolutely nothing he thought and then the realization slowly dawned on him. Snapping his head around he came face to face with what had been blocking him. Standing in the center of the courtyard was a young man in a black robe, the cowl lowered so Marcus couldn’t see his face.

Except for the lower half which was spread into a large grin. Of course he couldn’t sense anything he thougth, someone had been blocking him, but he was supposed to be a source Mage, there wasn’t supposed to be anyone on this planet who could do that save maybe Maelen he thought taking a step towards the mystery man standing stalwart and waiting.

“Marcus Gavin, it is truly a pleasure to finally catch up with you, you know I have been chasing you around and missing you by mere days, until that is I heard you were headed north and I also remembered that Veric was a friend. So, I took the gamble you would come to save him, and well here you are” The man said, not moving just standing there reguarding him from under the shadowed cowl.

Marcus felt anger began to well up in him the voices whispered danger, but he ignored them. “You didn’t have to kill him” Marcus growled taking another step. The robed figure simply shook his head. “Oh Marcus, haven’t you learned, the mundanes are merely on this earth to serve us, we are the true power, we are the ones who are meant to lead” he stated as if reciting some twisted doctrine. Pausing Marcus cocked his head and reguarded the figure. “What about the screamers, they weren’t mundane” he shot at him and he watched as the smile fell from his face.

“Sometimes sacrifices are necessary, they will be remembered as heroes of the cause Marcus, as will you my friend, it is truly an honor to be the one who captures you, the Empress will be so pleased” he said his smile returning. Marcus took another step “I am not caught yet” he growled gathering power to him as he took one last step. With a motion of his hand, he extended his hand. The focus run on the old leather glove glowed as he pushed a massive amount of kinetic force at the man. Then his eyes widened as the man merely moved his arm in a casual motion and the kinetic blast just simply dissipated. But that wasn’t what caught his attention was the cascade of power that lit the runes carved into the man’s body, even the robe couldn’t hide them from his sight. His entire body was covered head to toe with sigils that lit with power, quickly taking the initial weak instigation of magic and doubling it and then redoubling it and then again and again until it almost hurt Marcus to look at him. The tripe sigils engraved into his palm lit up as he made the casual motion dissipating the energy he had flung at the man.

The Robed figure shook his head in disapproval “That, Marcus was rude, we haven’t even been properly introduced” he said stepping to Marcus’s right, moving to block him from the entrance to the village, his only escape he noted. “What are you” Marcus asked not understanding what he had just seen, the voices in his head clamoring to offer there opinion, but again he quashed them, it was becoming easier to silence those voices he noticed, watching the man intently for signs he was gathering power but he was dark as he simply stood there, taking his hood down to show Marcus his obsidian eyes and wide smile. The black runes carved into his face a contrast to the pale white skin they framed.

“I am Juric Rogan Lord Seer of this land and one of the chosen of the Empress, you see Marcus” he began stepping again to the right casually continuing to put himself between marcus and his escape. “You see Marcus during the first Mage wars there was a scientist, a man with incredible vision but his methods were…” the Lord Seer contiuined, waiving his arm as he searched for the word. “rough, however the research results were incredible, they called him the harbinger of death as most of his subjects died on the table, but he found the way to increase magic in a subject, the Empress found the research and spent the last ten years working with it, The chosen are the culmination of that research” he continued spinning theatrically as he showed himself off.

“Before this, I could barely lift a pen with my power, but now, now I am more then a match for one like you, a source Mage” he said, Marcus concentrating on his words, he was caught utterly off guard when his runes flared and power shot out from him picking Marcus up before he could throw up a shield and sending him sailing into the side of the keep. He felt and heard bones break as he slammed into the stone wall, sliding down it to collapse at its base.

He tried to catch his breath, but everything hurt, he wasn’t able to take in a full lungful of air as the Lord Seer, Smiling slowly approached. Slowly climing to his feet, he stood there tensing himself for the next blow. “I am not sure what my Empress has planned for you Marcus but know your sacrifice will be heroic and you will be honored for generations” he said, and his tone was solemn. As his comment finished his runes flared again but this time Marcus was ready throwing up a shield of force as flame slammed into it, he felt the heat against his skin as Rogan continued to pour the flame at him. Marcus was hurt, weak and still new to his power, he felt the power diminishing as the shield began to weaken and finally fail as a jet of fire, hit his left shoulder burning the skin away, marcus screamed jumping out of the way of the fire and as he landed another pulse of kinetic energy hit him square on, sending him sliding into the stone well. More bones broke and he felt blood pour from his mouth as he coughed. “Oh, I might have been a little too rough, im sorry, we will get you looked after before delivering you to the Empress” Rogan said as he winced, his apology seeming almost authentic.

Marcus struggled to his feet, falling twice but finally standing as he used the edge of the well to hold him up. Summoning what power, he could he threw another jet of kinetic energy at the man, but it was weak as he began to fade, the pain and blood loss taking its toll. Rogan laughed shaking his head. “Honestly Marcus, I expected more from you” he said as he began to walk over to him. He took three steps and then as if a giant hand slapped him away, he flew into the side of the keep himself crumpling to the ground as he landed.

“Go Marcus, this fight is mine” Maelen said walking into the gate. Too weak to speak he tried to protest but the words failed him as Dara and Patrice ran over, helping him up. He looked over to the keep just in time to see Rogan stand, he favored his right side as he took a step towards Maelen. “That wasn’t fair, you’re not supposed to get in the middle of this old man” he said spitting blood on the ground to punctuate his words. “You are an abomination child, you will be dealt with” Maelen growled, reaching behind him and pulling the small silver staff, pulling it apart he flipped it holding the two parts like small clubs as he pointed the two crystal orbs and as they lit the sigils alighting along the hilt to Marcus’s eyes. Two blasts of energy shot into Rogan, lifting him off his feet once again and slamming him against the keep. Befure he hit, his arm extended backward, and power shot out dampening his strike.

“That’s how you want to play it” he grunted, getting up again. Rogan reached behind the robes pulling a similar weapon to Maelen’s, separating the two pieces he flipped one, so he held a long-handled blade in one hand and a crystal orb facing forward in the other. Maelen flipped his to bring forward the two blades. “This is how it is” he stated and looking quickly to the girls he made a motion “Get him out of here NOW”. They began to drag the Weakened Marcus as he tried to protest, tried to stop them but his loss of blood had made him incoherent. Rogan simply nodded to him as they walked past Maelen. “We will see each other soon my friend” he simply said and then focused on Maelen. The old man’s eyes burned with hate and power as he faced off with the Lord Seer.

As they carried him out Marcus turned to see the two Mages come together, metal and magic flashing as they struck and countered at speeds, he didn’t think was possible. Then he was beyond the fence, as they walked into the open field, the progress slow having to drag Marcus Dara gasped and Marcus followed her gaze. Soldiers, an entire line crested the hill and were riding down towards them. “We are trapped” Marcus croaked, knowing he was too beaten and too weak to help. Patrice turned to Dara “Make a kinetic bubble” she said, and the young girl nodded and with a pop they were inside a solid kinetic ball. Before Marcus could wonder what was happened. Patrice turned, thrusting out her hands and pushing against the fence. The wood creaked as the ball shot across the ground and through the soldiers, horses jumping out of the way as they slid over the inside surface and over the hill. Patrice pulled and extended her arms as she used trees and rocks, pushing against them to keep the ball rolling as Dara held it together.

Blue arcs of energy slammed into the ground near them as the soldiers fired, trying to slow or stop the mages, but the ball sped faster and faster careening across the fields. Again, dara gasped as she turned to look after a mile of field. Marcus turned trying to clear his blurring vision as he watched the treeline approach at breakneck speed. “Hold on” Patrice yelled, trying and failing to slow the kinetic ball as it slammed into the trees and went flying into the woods. Marcus slammed against the side of the kinetic ball and his world went black…
